audit.scope: Static review of docs/index.html, docs/case-study.html, and docs/site.css — focused on mobile accessibility cues: focus indication, touch target sizing, responsive layout, link clarity, heading/navigation structure, color reliance, and image alt text.
strengths: Semantic landmarks are present (header, main, footer) and primary navigation uses aria-label="Primary navigation".
Clear heading structure: each page has a single H1 and subordinate H2/H3 sections.
Responsive CSS: typography uses clamp(), grid.two collapses to one column in the @media (max-width: 43rem) rule, and actions use flex-wrap — generally mobile-friendly layout behaviour.
Primary CTA buttons have an explicit min-height (.button { min-height: 2.85rem; }) which meets common touch target height recommendations (~44px).
Images include alt text (case-study.html: img.case-visual alt describes the chart), supporting non-visual consumption of the key visual.
Active navigation state is exposed with aria-current="page" on the current nav link.

findings.evidence: site.css does not define any :focus or :focus-visible rules for interactive elements; buttons and links are styled but there is no custom focus styling (no selectors like a:focus, .button:focus, :focus-visible in site.css).
findings.risk: Keyboard and switch-device users (including some mobile assistive workflows) may have poor visibility of the currently focused element or inconsistent focus presentation across browsers; relying on default focus alone may be insufficient in some UA styles or when custom visuals overlap the outline.
findings.recommended_change: Add explicit, high-contrast focus styles (preferably using :focus-visible) for all interactive elements (a, .button, nav links, link-list items). Ensure the focus indicator is thick and has good contrast against the background and does not rely on color alone.

findings.evidence: nav a have no explicit padding (nav a { font-size: .85rem; text-decoration: none; }) and spacing is controlled by the nav flex gap. The header layout uses padding on the container but individual nav links lack a defined hit area.
findings.risk: Touch targets (especially narrow inline nav links) may be too small or too close together for comfortable and reliable tapping on small screens, increasing mis-taps for people with motor impairments.
findings.recommended_change: Increase the tappable area of navigation links by adding generous padding (eg. min-height >= 44px and horizontal padding), or convert nav links to buttons/blocks on small screens. Ensure a minimum reachable touch target of about 44 CSS pixels.

findings.evidence: nav a use color and removal of text-decoration (nav a { text-decoration: none; } and a { color: var(--teal); }) while only the current item gets an underline (nav a[aria-current="page"] { color: var(--ink); text-decoration: underline; }).
findings.risk: Link identity or state may be conveyed by color alone for many links (no underline or other non-color cue), which is problematic for users with color vision deficiencies or when color rendering is altered on-device.
findings.recommended_change: Provide a non-color indicator for links (for example keep an underline or add an icon/underline on focus/hover) and ensure the active state is perceivable without relying solely on color differences.

findings.evidence: Neither HTML file contains a ‘skip to content’ link or similar mechanism to move focus directly to main content (no visible first-link like Skip and main has no id used for skipping).
findings.risk: Keyboard and assistive-device users must tab through the header navigation on every page load, which increases time-to-content and friction on mobile keyboards or external keyboards paired to mobile devices.
findings.recommended_change: Add a skip link (visually hidden off-screen by default and visible on focus) pointing to the main element (give main an id) so users can jump straight to page content.

findings.evidence: .stat-value is styled with color: var(--coral) on card backgrounds that are white (stat-value { color: var(--coral); } and .card background: white). .notice uses border-left: 4px solid var(--coral) on a pale background.
findings.risk: Emphasis that relies primarily on a color (var(--coral)) may have insufficient contrast for some users or be lost to users with color deficiencies; numeric emphasis should remain perceivable to all users.
findings.recommended_change: Verify text/background contrast for var(--coral) and adjust if it falls below accessibility thresholds. Where possible, pair color emphasis with non-color cues (larger font-size, bold weight, icons, or borders) — note stat-value already uses large weight/size which helps, but contrast should be validated.

findings.evidence: Navigation is a bare set of anchor elements in the header (nav contains a sequence of <a> elements without an ordered list or increased hit-area), and there is no visible focus styling or skip link to aid keyboard navigation.
findings.risk: While semantics are present, small structural improvements (skip link, clearer grouping or increased hit areas) would reduce friction for users relying on keyboard navigation on mobile devices.
findings.recommended_change: Consider grouping nav items in a semantic list (<ul><li>) for clearer structure and add spacing/padding and focus styles to improve discoverability and operability for keyboard users.

limitations: Review limited to static source files provided (docs/index.html, docs/case-study.html, docs/site.css).
No testing on a physical mobile device, touchscreen, or with assistive technologies (screen readers) was performed.
No automated contrast calculation or runtime interaction testing was performed; recommendations are based on the static HTML/CSS observed.
